title: Scalar squares for supplied closed-test models
statement: Let $\Lambda,S$ be commutative condensed rings and $c:\Lambda\to S$ a morphism of ring objects [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Use the specified exact restriction of scalars, universal right-derived comparisons and section arrows [def-sfb-closed-test-scalar-comparison-maps] and the specified models and comparison maps [def-sfb-closed-test-scalar-model-diagrams]. Assume UniversalCoherence(c) and SectionCoherence(c). Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $a\subseteq A$ an ideal, $X$ affine, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $(h:X_Z\to X,f_Z:X_Z\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/a))$ the pullback of $f$ along the closed immersion [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $V$ be an affine pro-etale test over $\operatorname{Spec}(A/a)$ such that both $V$ and its specified closed-site lift are w-contractible [def-exc-closed-site-lift, sk-def-pe-wlocal]. For every bounded-below derived $S_X$-module $N$, TestModel $M$ of $N$ over $S$ and TestModel $P$ of $\operatorname{Res}_X N$ over $\Lambda$, ModelCoherence(c,A,a,f,h,f_Z,w,V,N,M,P) holds. All eight specified model arrows are isomorphisms, and the five specified scalar squares for source, target, chain restriction and localization commute. Only model and closed-unit isomorphisms are inverted.

proof.text: Use the K-injective section-model theorem for N and its scalar restriction, which is bounded below by exactness of restriction. Identify sourceModel with the inverse of the specified closed-unit inverse followed by the inverse direct-image section identity. Identify targetModel with the inverse of the right section identity followed by its computation-unit inverse. These give the first four IsIso clauses. Each localizationModel is the composite of an evaluation computation-unit iso on a K-injective complex, a derived localization iso, and the functor image of its representative iso, giving the remaining four. Restriction preserves the actual closed-unit section and its inverse. The assumed section and universal computation-unit equations, pasted with those section-model identities, give the source and target scalar squares. Only closed-unit and model isomorphisms are inverted.

source.place: Tag 09BL (lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply) (1)--(2); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6F for the normalized localized models.

proof.text: Identify the normalized exchanged arrow with Q of the actual unit section followed by j on the fibre, using the chain-mate restriction theorem. Paste the source and target scalar squares around the exchange square in the assumed UniversalCoherence. Cancel the normalized model isomorphisms to obtain exactly the chainRestriction square. The degreewise localization identity commutes with restriction; its computation-unit normalization and the same representative calculation give both localization squares, with the specified derived pullback/scalar compositor in the target.

proof.text: The universal, section and exchange equations used in the pasting are the assumed UniversalCoherence and SectionCoherence. A new Lambda-K-injective resolution of the restricted complex is used; restriction is never assumed to preserve K-injectives.

theorem closed_test_scalar_model_squares (hc : UniversalCoherence c) (hs : SectionCoherence c)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (a : Ideal A)
    {X XZ : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (h : XZ ⟶ X) (fZ : XZ ⟶ Spec (.of (A ⧸ a)))
    (w : IsPullback h fZ f (closedMap A a))
    (V : (Spec (.of (A ⧸ a))).AffineProEt)
    [IsWContractibleRing Γ(V.left, ⊤)]
    [IsWContractibleRing Γ((liftedTest A a V).left, ⊤)]
    (N : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj S X)))
    (M : TestModel S h N.obj) (P : TestModel Λ h ((restrict c X).obj N.obj)) :
    ModelCoherence c A a f h fZ w V N.obj M P
